issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the provided solution expect Stock.take(String) to return an int (using -1 to indicate failure), but the template implementation declares Stock.take(String) returning boolean. This mismatch prevents students from compiling or implementing SealSaloon logic that checks for -1 (e.g., if (stock.take(x) == -1) ...) and therefore blocks following the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template's Stock.take(String) method signature to return int (matching the UML and solution). Implement it to return -1 on failure (ingredient missing or insufficient quantity) and the remaining quantity (or appropriate non-negative value) on success, so students can check for -1 as specified in the problem and solution.

issues.description: Method signature mismatch for Stock.take: the problem statement UML and the solution implementation define Stock.take(String) to return an int (quantity or -1 on failure), but the template repository's Stock.take(String) returns a boolean. This inconsistency can confuse students about the expected contract of Stock.take and will cause compilation/behavior mismatches when they implement SealSaloon based on the problem description.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's Stock.take method signature match the problem statement and solution by changing its return type from boolean to int and using the same return conventions (e.g., return remaining quantity or -1 on failure). Update any template logic and usages accordingly so students can reliably map the specification to the provided code.
